In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of substitutional Si C alloys and SiC precipitates upon pulsed KrF excimer-laser annealing of carbon ion implanted silicon surfaces.
the development of novel laser processing methods for the preparation of Si C alloy films on Si surfaces.
the formation of epitaxial layers of silicon carbide on silicon substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of the epitaxial alloy is the dominating process in the concentration range of y 1 at%, whereas the formation of SiC precipitates dominates at concentrations of y 2 at%.
, depending on the implantation and laser processing parameters used, a wide range of carbon distributions can be obtained, ranging from epitaxial Si C alloy formation to Si C precipitation.
, in the investigated range, the carbon distribution in the Si C alloy matrix is controlled by the carbon concentration, the laser pulse duration, and the laser fluence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carbon redistribution process is a complex function of the implantation conditions as well as of the laser annealing process parameters.
the carbon ion implantation followed by KrF laser annealing is a powerful tool for the formation of SiC precipitates and epitaxial SiC alloy layers with high carbon content.

the carbon concentration in substitutional sites in the epitaxial Si 1 yCy alloy can be controlled by the implantation parameters, while the carbon content in precipitated SiC is controlled by the laser anneal parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pulsed excimer-laser annealing of ion-implanted SiC is a powerful tool for the preparation of epitaxial silicon carbide layers on Si substrates.
epitaxial Si 1 yCy alloys with y 1 at% can be grown on Si substrates by pulsed excimer-laser processing.

pulsed excimer lasers can be used for epitaxial Si C alloy formation and Si C precipitate nucleation and growth, and that the process is very sensitive to laser parameters and the implantation conditions.
